subject: SLA uptime anchoring & monthly credit smoothing — PriorityHealth
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@priorityhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: PriorityHealth Procurement <procurement@priorityhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification on uptime % and monthly credit cap for SOW

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the draft SOW. Before we loop legal, procurement has a couple of open items on the SLA:

- Uptime target: the draft references a 99.95% target for hosted. Procurement is trying to understand trade-offs vs a 99.9% anchor (cost sensitivity on our side). Can you confirm the operational/engineering changes that justify 99.95 over 99.9?
- Monthly credits: the SOW lists remedy bands but doesn't show a clear monthly cap. Our finance policy requires a hard cap (as a % of invoice) for commercial approval.
- Maintenance carveouts: we need narrower scheduled maintenance windows — our platform is customer-facing 24/7 and long maintenance windows are disruptive.
- Latency exceptions: can you confirm whether batched inference or prefix-caching behaviors could be excluded from latency SLAs? If so, we need explicit language.

I attached the latest SOW (v2) with a few inline notes. Can we have a short call today or tomorrow to resolve these so procurement can circulate a PO?

Attached: PriorityHealth_SOW_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Director, Cloud Procurement
PriorityHealth
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@priorityhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification on uptime % and monthly credit cap for SOW

Hi Elaine,

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers and a proposed offer below:

1) Uptime target: Redwood can commit to 99.95% availability for the hosted API (multi-AZ by default). The 99.95 figure reflects our regional redundancy model, proactive failover, and operational playbooks that materially reduce incident duration compared to 99.9. Practically, the difference is ~2.5x reduction in allowable downtime per month.

2) Monthly credits (proposed): remedy tiers based on monthly uptime percentage:
   - >=99.95%: no credit
   - 99.90–99.95%: 5% of monthly invoice
   - 99.0–99.90%: 15% of monthly invoice
   - <99.0%: 30% of monthly invoice
   Monthly cap: 25% of the monthly invoice.

3) Maintenance carveouts: default is scheduled maintenance (up to 4 hours/month) with 48 hours' notice. We'll consider tightening based on account profile.

4) Latency exceptions: batched inference/quantization fallbacks can affect p95 latency. We propose excluding latency credits when the customer enables aggressive batching/throughput-optimized profiles and acknowledges the tradeoff in writing (we can document via a config flag). For standard low-latency configs, latency remains within the SLA.

If that works as a starting point, I'll loop in Legal/Contracts and send a clean SLA PDF. If not, propose a 30-minute call tomorrow morning.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success – Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: internal: review PH counter / tighten maintenance language

Kimberly / Karthik / Marissa —

Reviewing Kimberly's proposed bands. A few internal asks from Legal/Contracts before we send the clean doc:

- Can we make scheduled maintenance a rolling quarterly allotment (e.g., 8 hours/quarter) rather than 4 hours/month? That gives ops scheduling flexibility but is easier to cap.
- Notice windows: recommend 14 days' notice for planned major maintenance; 48 hours for minor patching.
- Exclusions: be explicit that performance impact from customer-configured throughput/batching profiles is excluded only if customer toggles "throughput-optimized" in console and signs the config change form (clear audit trail).
- Monthly cap: Procurement may push back on 25%. Can we offer a stepped ramp: 15% cap for first 6 months of the contract, review at QBR, then 25% thereafter if utilization/support profile justifies?

Attaching a revised draft with inline redlines: redwood-sla-draft-202611.pdf

Laura
Director, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@priorityhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Revised SLA proposal and monitoring access

Hi Elaine —

Following internal review, here is an updated offer we can put into the SOW:

- Availability: 99.95% (hosted multi-AZ)
- Remedy bands: same as I outlined previously
- Monthly credit cap: 15% of the monthly invoice for the first six months; automatic re-evaluation at the first QBR with an option to move to 25% thereafter
- Scheduled maintenance: 8 hours per quarter; 14 days' notice for major windows, 48 hours for minor patching
- Latency carveout: customer-configured throughput/batching must be explicitly enabled via console and signed config change; only then are latency exceptions excluded
- Measurement: Redwood's telemetry will be primary for uptime calculation; we are open to symmetrically accepting external monitoring (PriorityHealth's probe logs) for reconciliation if there's a dispute — vendor-proof must be provided.

Attachments: clean SLA PDF and an operations note that describes the "throughput-optimized" toggle.

If this is acceptable, we can prepare the final SOW and a DocuSign envelope for signatures.

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Attachments referenced: redwood-sla-draft-202611.pdf
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@priorityhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: PriorityHealth Procurement <procurement@priorityhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Revised SLA proposal and monitoring access

Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick turn. Procurement reviewed the updated bands and we have one commercial counter: PriorityHealth policy caps monthly vendor liability (credits) at 10% of the invoice for contracted SaaS services unless escalated to our CFO. Can you accept a 10% flat cap with a carve for catastrophic (<99.0%) where we escalate to the CFO for exception?

Also:
- Maintenance: we can accept 8 hours/quarter but request that maintenance windows never be scheduled between 02:00–06:00 local on business-critical dates (we'll provide a calendar of blackout dates).
- External monitoring: we will provide probe logs (Pingdom) to reconcile, but expect that mutually agreed reconciliation windows are defined in the SOW.

Procurement has prepared a DocuSign envelope—link below—pending SLA confirmation.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/recipients/abc123-priorityhealth

Regards,
Elaine Park
Director, Cloud Procurement
PriorityHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: internal: final compromise for PH

Team — after reviewing Elaine's counter, recommended final position for commercial is:

- Accept 99.95% availability
- Monthly credit cap: 10% flat (to match procurement's policy) BUT add an extraordinary remediation path for <99.0% where credits are uncapped and we escalate to execs for a remediation/compensation plan (this aligns with risk management)
- Keep 8 hours/quarter scheduled maintenance with the blackout-date restriction; ops will maintain a shared calendar with PriorityHealth
- External monitoring reconciliation window: 7 days from the event (both parties submit logs)
- Latency carveouts: keep the signed-config toggle requirement

If legal signs off, we can accept these and Kimberly can approve final execution and ask Procurement to route the DocuSign. I'll attach the final PDF.

Marissa
VP, Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: final-sla-proposal-20261109.pdf

> Kimberly
